analysis:
I examined docs/reference/protocol-messages.md base lines 1-573. The PR only changes the drain section: base line 170 becomes head lines 170-174. The new text says a lifecycle drain on a provider with no registered session finishes without a coordinator `provider_drain_ack` once accepted work and local response writes finish. It cites `performLifecycleDrain` in provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/ProviderLoop+Lifecycle.swift.

This matches the surrounding text:
- A dead connection cannot deliver an acknowledgement (base 169-170).
- Unexpected transport loss keeps its cancellation paths (base 168-169).
- Restart or reconnect registers and authorizes a new connection (base 139-140).

The change does not alter any wire field, authorization, attestation, encryption or billing receipt semantics. The receipt claim still applies only when an ack is received (base 130-133). Base 148-150 says missing or late acknowledgements never imply success; the new case covers a provider with no session, where no coordinator fence or receipt exists. It does not claim the coordinator settled billing.

Relevant threat IDs are TB-002 (provider WebSocket), TB-011 and T-053 (connection-change lifecycle) and A-018 (serving availability). No regression was identified: the provider is adversarial and controls its own shutdown, and billing finality is coordinator-owned.

Open question for integration or code review: the Swift `performLifecycleDrain` implementation was not supplied. Integration should check that "no registered session" cannot be chosen while a live registered socket still has accepted inference. Otherwise an update could skip the barrier and cancel accepted work, which is an availability-only issue. Integration should also confirm that admission stays closed and that a skipped ack is never reported as a confirmed drain. This doc change does not establish either.
